# Medullary Breast Carcinoma

**Authors:** Faten Limaiem, Mouna Mlika

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Medullary carcinoma is a rare and distinct subgroup of breast carcinomas accounting for less than 5% of all invasive breast cancers. This unique histologic subtype has very strict criteria for diagnosis, including complete circumscription, the syncytial growth pattern of at least 75% of the tumor, intermediate to high nuclear grade, an associated diffuse lymphocytic infiltrate, and a lack of intraductal components or glandular differentiation. The 2012 World Health Organization (WHO) updated the classification of medullary carcinoma under the umbrella term “carcinomas with medullary features,” including atypical medullary carcinoma and invasive carcinoma of no special type with medullary features. Medullary carcinoma has a favorable prognosis despite its poorly differentiated histologic features and basal-like phenotype.
